data: 月曜[げつよう] 日[び]は １[いち]限[げん]しか 授業[じゅぎょう]が ありません。
I only have first period on Mondays.
限 · げん · College class periods, university class periods.
マフラーを 首[くび]に 2[に]巻[かん] きして 外[そと]に 出[で]た。
I wrapped the scarf around my neck twice and went outside.
巻/巻き · まき · How many times something has been rolled, wrapped or coiled around another thing.
この 教科[きょうか]書[しょ]の 第[だい]4[よん]版[ばん]を 持[も]っています。

版 · はん · Editions, impressions, printings, and magazine issues.
まずは 平仮名[ひらがな] ５０[ごじゅう] 音[おん]を 覚[おぼ]えましょう。

音 · おん · Sounds, such as syllables and/or musical notes.
社員[しゃいん] 規則[きそく]集[しゅう]の 第[だい]7[なな]則[そく]は 読[よ]みましたか?
Did you read the seventh rule of the employee rulebook?
則 · そく · This is an ordinal number suffix used to count rules.
マミの 成績[せいせき]は いつも クラスで ２[に]番[ばん]です。
Mami always gets the second-best grades in the class.
番 · ばん · 番 is an ordinal number suffix to show one's order, turn, or rank. It is common for 番 to be combined with another ordinal number suffix, 目 (め): 一番目, 二番目, etc.
ダリンは 1[いち]輪[りん]車[しゃ]に 乗[の]って 通勤[つうきん] している。
Darin comes to work by unicycle.
輪 · りん · Circles, rings, hoops, wheels, flowers (because the petals make a circle), and crowns of flowers.
この 建物[たてもの]には、 礼拝[れいはい]堂[どう]が 3[さん]堂[どう] あります。
In this building, there are three chapels.
堂 · どう · Chapels, temples, shrines, halls, lecture halls, auditoriums, assembly halls, churches, cathedrals, etc.
2[に]男[なん] 2[に]女[じょ]の 子供[こども]を 持[も]つ ことが 夢[ゆめ]なんです。
My dream is to have two sons and two daughters.

男 · なん · Sons. They're read using the kango readings, but two is an exception—instead of に, it's read as じ. It can also be used as an ordinal number suffix, but one and two become 長男 (ちょうなん) and 次男 (じなん).
運[うん] 悪[わる]く、 観光[かんこう] 客[きゃく]の 1[いち]団[だん]と 出[で]くわしてしまった。
Unfortunately, I ran into a group of tourists.
団 · だん · Orchestras, travelers, students, fellowships, troops, theatrical troupes, acting troupes, etc.
スポーツ 競技[きょうぎ] 会[かい]で、 ５[ご] 種目[しゅもく]の 競技[きょうぎ]に 出場[しゅつじょう] した。
In the sports competition, I participated in five different events.
種目 · しゅもく · Events during sporting competitions.
新築[しんちく] マンションが １２[じゅうに]戸[こ]売[う]りに 出[だ]されている。
Twelve new apartment units are for sale.
戸 · こ · Residential houses or apartment units. If you're counting buildings in general, regardless of whether or not they're home to the people inside, use the counter 軒 (けん) instead.
この 段落[だんらく]、 2[に] 段落[だんらく]に 分[わ]けた 方[ほう]が いいんじゃない?
Wouldn't it be better to separate this paragraph in two?
段落 · だんらく · Paragraphs and stages of tasks.
先週[せんしゅう]、 この 町[まち]で 殺人[さつじん] 事件[じけん]が ２[に]件[けん]も 起[お]きた そうです。
Apparently there were as many as two murders in this town last week.

件 · けん · Proposals, suggestions, legislative bills, agenda items, projects, plans, crimes, incidents, scandals, complaints, objections, contracts, agreements, emails, financing, loans, troubles, bankruptcies, page views, Internet access numbers, voice mail messages, etc.
この 歯[は] 医者[いしゃ]には、 いつも 週刊[しゅうかん]誌[し]が ４[よん]誌[し] 置[お]いてある。
This dentist always carries four different weekly magazines.
この 国[くに]に ある 1029[せんにじゅうきゅう]城[じょう]は、 全[すべ]て トーフグの ものだ。
All 1,029 castles in this country are Tofugu's.
城 · じょう · Castles, palaces.
44[よんじゅうよん]隊[たい]の 探検[たんけん]隊[たい]が この ジャングルで 行方[ゆくえ] 不明[ふめい]になった。
Forty-four expedition teams went missing in this jungle.
隊 · たい · Corps, units, parties, troops, and so on.
トイ・ ストーリー・ シリーズを、 2[に] 夜[よる] 連続[れんぞく]で お届[とど]けします。
We're going to air the Toy Story series two nights in a row.
夜 · や/よ · Nights. Normally, it's read with kango using the や reading for 夜, but one and two nights can also be counted with the wago readings. When that happens, 夜 becomes よ.
この プロジェクトを 達成[たっせい] するには、 2[に] 段階[だんかい]の フェーズが あります。
There are two phases to accomplishing this project.
段階 · だんかい · Steps—not stairsteps, but stages or phases.
この E ブックには、 トーフグの 短編[たんぺん]が 1029[せんにじゅうきゅう]編[へん] 収録[しゅうろく] されています。
This ebook contains 1,029 of Tofugu's short stories.
編/篇 · へん · Poems, pieces of writing, and other smaller units within the world of writing.
カナエの 机[つくえ]の 上[うえ]には、 88[はちじゅうはち]体[たい]の コウイチ 人形[にんぎょう]が 8[はち] 列[れつ]に 並[なら]べられていた。
On Kanae's desk, there were eighty-eight Koichi dolls arranged in eight lines.
列 · れつ · Lines or queues of people, rows of things in lines.

1[いち]筋[すじ]の 希望[きぼう]が 見[み]えてきたぞ。
I'm starting to see a single ray of hope.
筋 · すじ · Line, stripe, streak, crease, crack, wrinkle, or avenue.
私[わたし]は 日系[にっけい] ブラジル人[じん] 3[さん]世[せい]です。
９[きゅう]院[いん]で 院内[いんない] 感染[かんせん]が 発生[はっせい] している。
The hospital-acquired infection has appeared in nine hospitals.

院 · いん · Organizations or institutions whose names end with 院, including hospitals (病院/びょういん), temples or mosques (寺院/じいん), government houses like 上院/じょういん (Upper House) or 下院/かいん (Lower House), etc. One exception is 美容院 (びよういん), beauty salons. Because they're shops, they're counted with 軒 (けん).
折[お]り紙[がみ]で 5[ご] 弁[べん]の 花[はな]を 折[お]りました。
I made a five-petal origami flower.
弁 · べん · Petals that are still attached to a flower.
この 番組[ばんぐみ]から カップルが ３[さん]組[くみ] 誕生[たんじょう] した。

組 · くみ · Set, a group, or a pair of something. For one and two groups, use the wago reading (ひとくみ、ふたくみ). Three can be either (みくみ or さんさら). From four on up, just use kango. Quite commonly, you'll see 組 used to categorize classrooms too. When it's used this way, you just use kango. One class will be named ４組 (fourth class group), another ８組 (eighth class group).
新[しん]幹線[かんせん]の ひかり ４９３[よんひゃくきゅうじゅうさん]号[ごう]に 乗[の]りました。
I rode on the Shinkansen Hikari 493.
号 · ごう · 号 is an ordinal number suffix used for room numbers, train numbers, magazine volume numbers, and many other ordinal numbers. Inexplicably, it's also a unit for canvas sizes.
アヤは アメリカの 大統領[だいとうりょう]を ２[に]期[き] 務[つと]めた。
Aya served two terms as President of the United States.
期 · き · 期 is a fairly formal counter used to enumerate terms and periods.
敵国[てきこく]の ３[さん] 軍[ぐん]が こちらへ 向[む]かっている そうだ。
I hear three enemy armies are headed our way.
軍 · ぐん · Army groups, groups of troops, sports team levels, baseball team levels, etc.
とても 美[うつく]しい 桜[さくら]の 花[はな]ですね。 １[いち] 枝[えだ] 分[わ]けてもらえませんか？
Such beautiful cherry blossoms. May I take a branch?

枝 · えだ · Branches with flowers, fruit, or elegant leaves on them. For bare branches, you can use the long stick Japanese counter 本 (ほん), and for one and two, count with the wago counting method. For the rest, use kango.
俳句[はいく]は 五[ご] 文字[もじ]、 七[なな] 文字[もじ]、 五[ご] 文字[もじ]で 書[か]かないといけません。
You need to write haiku with a five-seven-five syllable count.
文字 · もじ · Letters, characters, morae in poetry.
新[あたら]しい トーフグの ステッカーの アイディアを １０[じゅう] 案[あん] 提出[ていしゅつ] した。
I submitted ten new Tofugu sticker design ideas.

案 · あん · Plans, ideas, projects, and strategies. While you can also use the 〜つ counter to count these things, you'll probably hear 案 used more often in business situations. Count all 案 numbers with kango.

高級[こうきゅう] 時計[とけい] ５[ご]点[てん]が 盗[ぬす]まれた。

点 · てん · Items, scores, dots, points, fulcrums, and any kind of artwork including paintings, sculptures, literature, and even films. When counting scores, 点 can be applicable to the score of a sports game as well as your score on a test.
ガスタンク ４[よん]基[き]が 爆発[ばくはつ] した。
基 · き · Installed things that are big or hard to move. Pyramids, ancient tombs, tombstones, gravestones, coffins, moai statues, torii gates, etc.
靴下[くつした] ３[さん]足[そく]で ５００[ごひゃく]円[えん]だって。
It says three pairs of socks for ¥500.
足 · そく · Pairs of shoes, slippers, sandals, boots, socks, and so on.
瓶[びん] ビール 4[よん] 瓶[びん]も 空[あ]けたの!?
Did you empty four whole beer bottles!?
瓶 · びん · Glass bottles, glass jars, flagons, decanters, phials, and vials.
刺[さ]し身[み]を 4[よん] 舟[ふね] 頼[たの]んでおいたよ。
I ordered four boats of sashimi ahead of time.
舟 · ふね · Boats and food in boat-shaped serving dishes.
港[みなと]に 3[さん]隻[せき]の 船[ふね]が 停泊[ていはく] していた。
There were three ships anchored in the port.
隻 · せき · Big ships. Small boats use 艘 (そう).
ジュースを ９[きゅう]杯[はい]も おかわり した。
I refilled my juice as many as nine times.

杯 · はい · Liquids in cups or bowls. That means you can count things like bowls of soup, mugs of coffee, glasses of juice, measuring spoons of vanilla, measuring cups of chicken broth, and so on. In addition, you can use 杯 to count squid, cuttlefish, crabs, and sometimes octopuses. 杯 can also count ships, battleships, racing yachts, and other boats, but this usage isn't so common.
この 家[いえ]には 寝室[しんしつ]が ３[さん] 部屋[へや] あります。
There are three bedrooms in this house.
部屋 · へや · Rooms. For one, two, and sometimes three rooms, use the wago counting method. Beyond that use kango.
３[さん]泊[ぱく] ４日[よっか]で 東京[とうきょう] 旅行[りょこう]に 行[い]ってきた。
I went on a three-night and four-day trip to Tokyo.
泊 · はく · Overnight stays or rentals.
その 年[とし]は、 ５[ご]行[ぎょう]の 銀行[ぎんこう]が 倒産[とうさん] した。
That year five banks went bankrupt.
行 · こう · Banks, groups of people, parties of people.
刺[さ]し身[み]、 ３[さん]切[き]れしか 残[のこ]ってないの？
Are there only three pieces of sashimi left?
切れ · きれ · Cut/sliced things (especially foods). You'll see this used to count slices of sashimi or filets of meat, for example.
答[こた]えを 書[か]き込[こ]む マスは 5[ご] マスです。
There are five blanks for you to fill in the answer.
升/枡 · ます · Squares or boxes on paper, blank spaces, masu cups.
お好[この]み焼[や]き ソースを 2[に] 刷毛[はけ] 塗[ぬ]った。
I smeared on two strokes of okonomiyaki sauce.
刷毛 · はけ · Brush strokes.
１人[ひとり]で ポテチを ２[に]袋[ふくろ]も 食[た]べちゃった。
I ended up eating two whole bags of potato chips all by myself.
袋 · ふくろ · Bags, sacks, pouches. For one or two bags, use the wago counting scheme (ひとふくろ, ふたふくろ). After that use kango.
受付[うけつけ]に お約束[やくそく]の 御[ご]２[に] 方[ほう]が お見[み]えです。
There are two people in reception who have an appointment.
方 · かた · People (formal). For one, two, and three people, you'll want to attach the prefix 御 (お). You can also refer to a group of people of an unknown number using 方.
あの 選手[せんしゅ]は、 1[いち] 試合[しあい]で 合計[ごうけい] 7[なな]盗[とう] した。
That player stole seven bases in one game.
盗 · とう · Steals (of bases) in baseball.
ツナ 缶[かん] ５[ご]缶[かん]と コーラ １２[じゅうに]缶[かん]を 買[か]った。
I bought five cans of tuna and twelve cans of cola.

缶 · かん · This word means can (as in an aluminum can). Its reading is (coincidentally) "kan", and it can be used to count cans. The first two cans can be counted with either wago or kango numbers. "One can" is １缶, read as either いっかん or ひとかん. "Two cans" is ２缶, read as either にかん or ふたかん. From three cans and up you use the kango counting method. When a can is empty—or when it's a garbage can—you'll generally want to use the counter 個 instead of 缶.
